text:
dina: Quick q on Persephone-3.2 license — can we ship quantized weights to a customer for Private deployment?

mike: Are we talking about providing the .pt/.bin after quantization, or running conversion on their infra?

dina: Providing a pre-quantized binary that they'd load into a BYO cluster (customer has air-gapped). License attached below. Trying to avoid legal surprises before we start evals.

dina: Excerpt:
```
Section 2. Redistribution: No distribution of model weights or derivative weights is allowed without explicit permission from Acacia Labs. Serving the model as an API is permitted.
Section 4. Attribution: All public use must display: "Persephone-3.2 (c) Acacia Labs" and link to upstream.
```

mike: Ok — that wording is pretty restrictive. Two quick notes: (1) quantized weights are almost certainly a derivative; (2) shipping the binary = redistribution.

jane_legal: Yep — short version: if the upstream license says "no redistribution of model weights or derivative weights" then providing a quantized file to a customer is redistribution and is disallowed unless you have a written exception from the model owner.

ashley: What if we package the model in a container that pulls weights at first-run from customer's own credentials (they download from the model hub)? We wouldn't touch the weights.

jane_legal: That pattern can work. If the customer obtains weights directly from the upstream source under their own account and we only provide orchestration/runtime, we're not redistributing. But two caveats: (a) we must not cache or store copies of the weights in our control plane; (b) we must avoid transferring a copy through our infra.

sam: In practice we do a BYOW flow already for other models: installer script checkssum's the artifact and references a local path. Ops note: need an offline flow for air-gapped customers too.

license-bot: Automated scan: Persephone-3.2 license flagged: "redistribution_prohibited", "attribution_required", "derivative_restrictions"

mike: Another wrinkle: quantization itself is a transformation. Legal treats it as creating a derivative. So even if the customer provides FP32 weights and we run quantization on-prem for them, that might be allowed (we're not distributing the quantized artifact), but shipping the quantized artifact is not.

dina: So recommended approaches?

jane_legal: Options ranked: 
1) BYOW — customer downloads upstream weights and we orchestrate (best if license forbids redistribution).
2) Get explicit written permission from Acacia Labs to redistribute quantized weights (needs legal to negotiate).
3) If the license permits derivatives but requires attribution, include a compliance header and docs.

jane_legal: Example compliance header we should surface in docs (and in the UI when enabling this model):
```
Model: Persephone-3.2
Upstream: Acacia Labs (https://acacia.example/persephone)
License: Non-Redistribution v1.0 — attribution required
Notes: Quantized weights are derivative artifacts. Redistribution prohibited unless explicit permission granted.
```

ashley: For Dedicated or Hosted customers who want us to manage weights, we need to gate onboarding: if license forbids redistribution, disallow us storing or serving their copy. If they want us to host, we either need permission or we refuse.

sam: Action items: (1) I'll add a BYOW option to the persephone eval runbook and an airgap doc. (2) @jane_legal can you open a ticket to request a redistribution exception if product wants us to offer pre-quantized packages?

jane_legal: Will do. Also recommend we add an automated check in our model onboarding flow to flag any license that mentions "redistribute", "derivative", or "no commercial use" so eng/SEs see it earlier.

mike: Thanks. Also: we should add an eval note — don't include quantized binaries in public eval artifacts (e.g., GH releases).

dina: Sounds good. I'll update the onboarding doc and mark Persephone-3.2 as BYOW-only until legal confirms.

sam: I'll file the GH issue for the automation rule and link here.

license-bot: Ticket created: #ML-lic-412 (request to Acacia Labs for redistribution exception)

dina: Great, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
